title: Earnings and entry wealth: decision review
date: September 22, 2026 | Prepared for the 21:00 EDT discussion
summary: Experimental comparison against this morning's V5 diagnostic: A/B use one persistent earnings shock; C/D retain persistent plus iid risk, with their corresponding stationary entrant-income distributions. A/C enter with zero assets; B/D use the inherited heterogeneous wealth marginal. All keep the age profile, timing, current-income purchase eligibility, housing-floor/equivalence-scale forms, transfer rules, targets and weights. Income resolution changes; the wealth grid is unchanged. Searches vary nine parameters and re-normalize the fertility utility scale. None is paper adoption.

All 163 attempted coarse-grid objectives passed; 81 planned proposals were unrun within the fixed budgets. The persistent-only process also passed at 15 states with both entry-wealth assumptions. Zero entry wealth is therefore not necessary to make that specification solve.

The best observed persistent-only, heterogeneous-wealth point still predicts 45.3% ownership versus 64.8%, 6.25 rooms versus 5.56, and a 1.34-room first-birth response versus 0.72. The same main housing misses appear across the four specifications.

Seven states are not yet an adequate numerical certificate: moving to 15 delays mean first birth by 0.52-0.55 years at common search parameters. At 45 states, the zero-wealth two-component case timed out; the heterogeneous-wealth case failed the unchanged feasibility gate at a tiny population mass.
recommendations: Use one persistent earnings process plus the age profile as the working baseline direction. Retain heterogeneous entry wealth, after harmonizing its income definition. Verify the selected point at richer resolution and assess continuation feasibility; then settle the housing-floor versus child-share specification before a long calibration.
limitations: The inherited wealth proxy mixes family-income and model earnings denominators and uses a diagnostic rank coupling. Four-year income is known at the decision; entry income risk is stationary at age 18. Grid robustness and exact selected-point repetitions remain unproved. The parenthood housing floor is at its 2.3 upper bound in all selected points. Lower weighted loss is not an adopted fit. Some original appendix legends overlap or clip; their source images are preserved and flagged.
